title: fix(metadata-protocol): duplicatePackage points a copied permission set's field-level rules at the copied objects
body:
Fixes #23527
Clause-②: no

## What this does

`duplicatePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, ADR-0070 D4) promises to rewrite "every intra-package reference". A permission set's field-level rules are `PermissionSetSchema.fields`, a record whose key is documented as `ENTITY_NAME.FIELD_NAME` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`). Since PR #23525 a copied set's `objects` keys followed the renamed objects, but its `fields` keys still named the SOURCE objects. The security plugin reads a set's rules for an object by the key prefix `OBJECT.` (`PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions`), so the copy's field rules governed the source's objects and the duplicate's objects got none.

Now, in the `duplicatePackage` region only, a narrow step beside `deepRewrite` (`rewriteFieldRuleKeys`) rewrites the `fields` keys of every copied `permission` item:

- **The split rule (H2).** The object part of a key is everything before its FIRST `.`. It is rewritten only when it equals a renamed object name exactly, through the same `renameMap` the objects take. The field part is never read. `dupsrc_customer.full_name` becomes `dupdst_customer.full_name`; `ticket.title` (a bare object, renamed by #23511 to `dupdst_ticket`) becomes `dupdst_ticket.title`; `ticket.ticket` becomes `dupdst_ticket.ticket`; a key naming an object outside the package keeps its name.
  - Why the first dot is safe: an object name is `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` (`ObjectSchema.name`) and so is a field name (the `ObjectSchema.fields` record key and `FieldSchema.name`), so neither can hold a `.`.
  - It is the split both readers already use. The evaluator matches `startsWith(OBJECT + '.')`, and the `security-fls-unknown-field` lint splits "on the FIRST dot", saying that this "mirrors that evaluator exactly". A key with a second dot keeps its whole remainder as the field part, which is also what both readers do.
- **Keyed on the declared shape, not on a property name.** The step reads only the `fields` record of a copied `permission` item. A property-name rule would also catch an object's own `fields` (keyed by field name). The code comment says why `deepRewrite` and the derived site index do not carry it. Measured with the index: it reads `permission.fields` as a site naming `field` items (the property spells that type), never `object`, and it has no arm for a composite key. Widening the index would also change the "Used by" answer it feeds. `reference-sites.ts` is untouched.
- **A collision is refused, never merged.** If a rewritten key equals a key the set already holds (the source set also has a rule for an object outside the package that is named like the copy), keeping either rule would silently drop the other. The set is reported in `failed[]` with both keys and the remedy, and nothing is written for it. This is the same posture as the claimed-name refusal from PR #23525. Measured reachable: the save door accepted a source set holding both `dupsrc_customer.full_name` and `dupdst_customer.full_name`.
- The `duplicatePackage` docblock gains one sentence on the `fields` keys. No other region of `protocol.ts` is touched (`git diff` is +70 / -0 lines, all in the method). The source-row `where` line PR #23469 edits is untouched.

## Zone 2 hypotheses, measured on a real kernel (ObjectKernel + ObjectQLPlugin, memory driver)

- **H1 holds.** At `b1cfa3d26`, the new pin file's base run had 4 of 4 cases red, both arms. The copied set's keys were exactly the source's: `dupsrc_customer.full_name`, `ticket.title`, `ticket.ticket`, and so on. `failed` was `[]`. `deepRewrite` renames a record key only under an object-reference property, and the free-text regex reads values, never keys.
- **H2 holds, with one measured interaction (see Acceptance notes).** No field name can hold a `.`. On the bare arm, a field part that spells the object's name stays and copies end to end. On the prefixed arm, the object copy itself half-renames such a field, which is a separate pre-existing defect handed to the seat.
- **H3: the enumeration is below.** Only `PermissionSetSchema.fields` is fixed here.
- **H4 holds, measured through the consumer's own functions.** A one-off measurement in `plugin-security` (not committed) read the stored copied set with `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` and `FieldMasker.maskResults`, the pair the read path composes (`security-plugin.ts`, `getFieldPermissions` then `maskResults`).
  - At head, for a holder of the copied set, `dupdst_customer` resolves `{ full_name: { readable: false, editable: false } }` and the masked record drops `full_name`. `dupdst_ticket` drops `secret`.
  - With the key rewrite ablated (the base behaviour for keys), both objects resolve `{}`. Both records come back whole: `full_name: "Ada"` and `secret: "s3cret"` are readable.
  - The full HTTP middleware path was not driven.

## H3: other composite forms naming an object in copied items

Method: a grep of `packages/spec/src` for composite key and value forms that name an object (`OBJECT.FIELD`, `OBJECT.VIEWKEY`, `OBJECT.NAME`), read with the derived site index's `permission` rows (`object` from `object` and `objects`; `field` from `fields`; `position` from `positions`). These were found:

1. **`permission.fields` keys, `OBJECT.FIELD`.** Fixed here.
2. **Stored view-item row NAMES, `OBJECT.VIEWKEY`** (`ViewItemNameSchema`: "the object can be recovered from the prefix"). Measured on a real kernel: a bare object's view item `ticket.board` is copied under the same name, `ticket.board`, bound to the target, while its `object` becomes `dupdst_ticket`. A read naming no package serves the source's row (`object: ticket`). The prefixed case is consistent (`dupsrc_customer.board` becomes `dupdst_customer.board`). Out of scope; handed to the seat.
3. **Values that carry a view-item id, `OBJECT.VIEWKEY`** (for example a form-view target). A prefixed name is rewritten by the free-text regex. A bare name is rewritten only as a whole value at an object-reference property, so `ticket.board` inside such a value stays. Read from the code, not measured; noted only.
4. **`field` item names, `OBJECT.NAME`.** The runtime-create door is retired (`allowRuntimeCreate: false`), so no package-held row is expected. Not measured.
5. **Not composite:** translation `objects` (keyed by a bare object name, already covered by PR #23525's record-key rule; its nested `fields` are keyed by field name) and the dashboard filter's translation-bundle lookup (a resolution path, not a stored key).

## Pins

New file: `packages/objectql/src/protocol-duplicate-package-permission-field-keys.test.ts`, beside `protocol-duplicate-package-unprefixed-object.test.ts`. It reads the stored rows out of the driver, never a payload. The base column was read against a `metadata-protocol` dist built at `b1cfa3d26`, using the first fixture revision (the field-part case then used `dupsrc_customer.dupsrc_customer`; see Acceptance notes). The ablation column used the final fixture.

| case | at `b1cfa3d26` | key rewrite ablated | at head |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| a prefixed object's key follows, with its rule. NEGATIVE CONTROL: no key of the copy names `dupsrc_customer` | red | red | green |
| a bare object's key follows to the target-namespace name. NEGATIVE CONTROL: no key of the copy names `ticket` | red | red | green |
| only the object part moves: `ticket.ticket` and `dupsrc_customer.ticket` become `dupdst_ticket.ticket` and `dupdst_customer.ticket`. NEGATIVE CONTROL: no `dupdst_ticket.dupdst_ticket` and no `dupdst_customer.dupdst_ticket` | red | red | green |
| a key naming an object outside the package (`dupext_account.name`, a third package's object) keeps its name; the full key set; the source set untouched | red | red | green |
| a renamed key that meets a key the set already holds is refused at the set, naming both keys and the remedy. NEGATIVE CONTROL: nothing of the set was written to the target, and the object still copied | not run (case added after the base run; at base no key moves, so nothing collides) | red | green |

## Ablation (one, on the key rewrite)

- **The mutation.** The `renameMap.get(key.slice(0, dot))` lookup in `rewriteFieldRuleKeys` was changed to `renameMap.get('ABLATED_23527_' + key.slice(0, dot))`, so no key is renamed. It ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor x1 to x0, blob `776cba82b` to `15af0f8e4`.
- **The ablated run.** After a `metadata-protocol` rebuild, `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 2 dist files. The pin went 5 failed / 0 passed, each for the base reason (`expected undefined`, the source key set, `failed` of length 0). The H4 measurement ran in the same state.
- **The restore.** The tool proved it: the blob equals HEAD `776cba82b`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. After a rebuild, `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` found the marker in none of 24 dist files and the working tree clean against HEAD. The pins went 9 passed, the 5 new ones plus the 4 in `protocol-duplicate-package-unprefixed-object.test.ts`.

## Tests and gates (at `ee862ff9d`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 236 files passed, 3 skipped; 28408 tests passed, 19 skipped (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 418 files, 8108 tests passed (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
- `metadata-protocol` typecheck: exit 0.
- `objectql` typecheck: exit 0, and `check:test-typecheck` is OK with its debt unchanged. The new file is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 67 families at `ee862ff9d`. All were run locally, and `--ran` with recorded exit codes reconciles: 67 derived, 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
  - `check:lean-entry-closure` first refused its prerequisite. It reran with exit 0 after an `objectql` build.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is NOT MEASURED: `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3), because it needs the whole workspace built. It is left to CI.
- `origin/main` has moved one commit (`e1cefa58e`, the hono adapter and its conformance test), which is disjoint from this diff. `git merge-tree` is clean. No merge was made; the PR's merge-ref CI covers the joint state.

## Acceptance notes

- **A field part that spells a PREFIXED object's name is refused at the copy. This comes from a separate defect, not from this rule.** Measured on a real kernel:
  - The object copy's free-text regex rewrites a field's `name` value but not its `fields` record key. A field keyed `dupsrc_customer` is copied as key `dupsrc_customer` with `name: 'dupdst_customer'`, and `x_dupsrc_customer` gets `name: 'x_dupdst_customer'`.
  - The data plane addresses the column by the key. An insert with `dupsrc_customer` is stored; one with `dupdst_customer` is refused `INVALID_FIELD Unknown field 'dupdst_customer' on object 'dupdst_customer'`.
  - So the rule here (`dupsrc_customer.dupsrc_customer` becomes `dupdst_customer.dupsrc_customer`) names the right column. But the save door's `security-fls-unknown-field` lint reads the half-renamed `name`, so such a copied set is now listed in `failed[]` (`failed author-time validation … [security-fls-unknown-field]`).
  - Before this change, the same set copied with every key naming the source objects. It was fail-open for all its rules, not just that one.
  - The pins avoid such a field and say why in the fixture's comment. The upstream defect is handed to the seat.
- **Read only, not measured:** a view-item id inside a value (H3 item 3) keeps a bare object's name.

## Out of scope, handed to the seat (measured; not fixed here)

1. The object copy half-renames a field whose name ends in a prefixed object name (above).
2. **`objects`-key collision (PR #23525's record-key rule).** A source set holding `objects: { dupsrc_customer: { allowRead }, dupdst_customer: { allowRead, allowEdit, allowDelete } }` copies with `failed: []` as `objects: { dupdst_customer: { allowRead, allowEdit, allowDelete } }`. One grant is dropped silently, and here the copied object gains edit and delete that the source set never granted on its own object.
3. A bare object's view-item row keeps its `OBJECT.VIEWKEY` name (H3 item 2).
4. **"Used by" misses a set that names an object only in `fields` keys.** `findReferencesToMeta` for object `dupsrc_customer` lists `permission/dupsrc_objects@objects{key}` but not a saved set whose only reference is `fields: { 'dupsrc_customer.full_name': … }`. This is the measurement the dispatch asked for.
